label: prop:delta-lambda-dt-index-unification
title: $\Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda$ is a DT/3d-index Euler characteristic with geometric chirality
html:
Proposition. \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda is a DT/3d-index Euler characteristic with geometric chirality

Proposition. Let \lambda be a partition, written as a weakly decreasing list, with a-function grade n(\lambda) and Wedderburn dimension \dim V_\lambda. Set

  \Delta_\lambda \;=\; (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\,\dim V_\lambda .

Then both factors are identified with independently-defined objects:

  1. (value) the DT / 3d-index Euler characteristic on the graded pieces equals \Delta_\lambda,
  \sum_{k=0}^{n(\lambda)} (-1)^k \dim \mathrm{gr}_k
  \;=\; (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\,\dim V_\lambda ;
  1. (chirality) the a-function parity equals the geometric longest-element sign,
  (-1)^{n(\lambda)} \;=\; (-1)^{\sum_i \binom{\lambda'_i}{2}} ,

where \lambda' is the conjugate partition. Both hold for every n, with no restriction.

Why this is a theorem and not a definition

Writing \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda by itself asserts nothing — it names a product of a sign and a dimension. The content is that neither factor is free:

  • the magnitude is forced as an Euler characteristic, an alternating sum over the graded pieces, rather than being posited as the Wedderburn dimension;
  • the sign is forced as a geometric invariant — the longest-element sign of the associated Weyl-group datum — rather than being posited as the jet-order parity.

The bridge between the two readings of the sign is the combinatorial identity n(\lambda) = \sum_i \binom{\lambda'_i}{2}, which is what removes the earlier n \le 5 restriction: the chirality leg had been established only for small n until that identity was proved in general.

Lean

QOU.BraidsAndKnots.dtEuler_eq_deltaLambda_unconditional states the conjunction of both legs and is sorry-free. The value leg is dtEulerG_eq_deltaLambdaG; the chirality leg is parity_eq_w0_sign_general, which discharges (\dagger) via aStat_eq_sumChoose2_conjugate.

Scope — the value only

This fixes the per-partition value. It does not address the many-body binding magnitude, which remains open: no per-block weight converts an intensive quantity into an extensive one, so the missing contribution is a separate additive extensive term rather than a different choice of \Delta_\lambda. Six closure ansätze have failed on the deuteron for exactly that reason. Nothing here should be read as narrowing that gap.

Consumers

The per-isotope binding algorithm consumes \Delta_\lambda through alg:delta-lambda-closure, which computes the value above and hands it to Step 9b.
